topic: Turning on two-step verification for your most important account, like email, for extra protection
headline: Add A Second Lock To Email
supporting_text: Turn on two-step verification so a stolen password alone can't get someone in.
caption:
⚡ TODAY’S 30-SECOND TECH WIN

Your email account is often the key to everything else — if someone gets into it, they can reset passwords for your other accounts too.

Two-step verification adds a second lock. Even if someone learns your password, they also need a code sent to your phone or email to get in.

Open your email app or account website, look in Settings for "Security" or "Sign-In," and look for an option like "Two-Step Verification" or "Two-Factor Authentication." Turn it on and follow the prompts.

It takes under a minute, but it can make your account much harder to break into.

Save this tip for later.

Follow @DigitalCalmDaily for one simple 30-Second Tech Win every day.
visual_symbol: a padlock with a small shield behind it
reel_hook: Give your email a second lock
reel_steps: Open your email app or account website
Go to Settings, then Security or Sign-In
Find Two-Step Verification and turn it on
Follow the prompts to add a phone or backup email
